profiles.name: DREADFUL
profiles.profile: This file is basically a police report on the wedges and the flatstick. The driver isn’t the main villain here; it’s the whole middle-and-end-of-the-hole operation collapsing like a cheap lawn chair. There are flashes where the ball actually goes somewhere useful, but the scoring clubs keep setting fire to the good work with chunked recoveries and too many extra taps. When the putter heats up, it’s more of a small space heater than a rescue mission. Very volatile, very ugly, and somehow still hanging around the top of the card.

profiles.name: tnboles77
profiles.profile: This is the kind of player who can look cooked and still somehow cash a clean one when the window opens. The long game has enough punch to get attention, but the contact quality on approaches and the general error load keep dragging the round back into the mud. When it does click, it’s because the putter and short game drag the corpse across the finish line. The profile is mixed: one week he’s a grindy bastard, the next he’s donating strokes like a man with a vendetta against momentum.

profiles.name: IUDoc92
profiles.tagline: THE FIGHT IS WITH THE SHORT GRASS
profiles.profile: This is a hard file to love because the tee ball keeps writing bad checks and the rest of the bag spends the round trying to cover rent. There are enough bright shots to keep him from looking totally lost, but the penalty for one sloppy hole is usually a whole damn avalanche. The weird part is that the putter can show up just enough to make the damage feel avoidable, which is somehow more irritating. The golf is volatile, but the recurring shape is clear: too much scrambling, not enough clean tee-to-green work.

profiles.name: MashedBROtato
profiles.tagline: BOOM OR BUST WITH A SIDE OF CHAOS
profiles.profile: This dude has a proper hammer in the bag, and then immediately follows it with a shovel. The driver can absolutely show up and bully a hole, but the rest of the round keeps sneaking into the kitchen and stealing the groceries. There are enough peaks here to explain the one clean win, yet the recurring issue is that the approach game and the scoring cleanup work don’t always cash the same check. When the putter cooperates he looks dangerous; when it doesn’t, the scorecard starts looking like a tax form written by a raccoon.

profiles.name: Jakobm90
profiles.profile: There’s real ceiling here, mostly because the tee ball can get loud in a hurry. The problem is that the rest of the bag often arrives at the party after the damage is already done, and the approach work can absolutely throw a chair through the window. Still, this one can spike a round when the putter and short game decide to stop being freeloaders. It’s not clean, but it is alive, and that matters in a league where a few holes of competence can fake respectability.

profiles.name: Leroy4522
profiles.tagline: APPROACH GAME IN A BODY BAG
profiles.profile: The recurring problem here is painfully simple: the tee ball gives you just enough hope, and then the irons walk in and mug it in an alley. There’s enough short-game scrapiness to stop total collapse from becoming the default, but the approach numbers keep dragging this profile back into the basement. Every now and then the putter bails out a mess and makes it look less gruesome than it was. This is a mixed file with one very obvious villain, and the villain wears cleats and carries a mid-iron.
